parsedVerdict.reasoning: Claim.ts is a domain entity, and all of its code is domain work. It holds claim state (id, policyNumber, peril, incidentOn, claimedCents, status, paidCents). It also enforces business rules: settle() checks that the claim is open, works out the payout as the claimed amount minus the deductible, capped at the limit, and moves the status to settled. decline() makes the same open-status check before moving to declined. Errors are raised as DomainError, and amounts use the Money value object from the shared kernel. The file has no persistence code, such as ORM decorators, repository calls or SQL. It has no transport or presentation code, such as HTTP status codes, DTO mapping or serialization, and no framework code. The public mutable fields are a weakness in encapsulation, but they don't put another layer's work into this file. Persistence lives in the separate infrastructure files (InMemoryClaimRepository, TypeOrmClaimRepository), which is the right place for it.
